report.summary: The only failure is test_invalid_book_is_rejected[blank-title], which expects a whitespace-only title to be rejected with 422 but gets 201 Created. The app's title check at app/main.py:75 uses `if not book.title`, which does not catch whitespace, while the author check on line 77 uses `.strip()`. Fix the title validation in app/main.py to strip before checking; the test is correct and no test change is needed.

causes.title: Whitespace-only book titles are accepted by validate_book
causes.explanation: validate_book only rejects an empty title (`not book.title`). A title of "   " is truthy, so it passes validation and the API stores the book with a 201 response. The author check on the next line already uses `.strip()`, so the title check is inconsistent with the intended rule of rejecting blank values. This is deterministic and does not depend on timing or data outside the request, so it is a product bug and the test is right to fail. The other three parametrized cases (empty-author, next-year, year-zero) are not in the failure list and therefore passed.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:63-66: test sends {"title": "   ", "author": "A"} and asserts `response.status_code == 422`; error is `assert 201 == 422`
app/main.py:74-76: `def validate_book(book: BookIn) -> None:` / `if not book.title:` / `raise HTTPException(422, "Title must not be blank")`
app/main.py:77: `if not book.author.strip():` shows the author check strips whitespace but the title check does not
app/main.py:69: `title: str` with no min_length or strip validator on BookIn, so whitespace reaches validate_book unchanged
causes.suggested_fix: In app/main.py validate_book, change line 75 to `if not book.title.strip():` so that whitespace-only titles raise HTTPException(422, "Title must not be blank"). Consider also stripping stored titles so "  Dune " is normalized. Then rerun tests/api/test_books_api.py, including the blank-title case.
